doc.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997

title: Recording with other baritone saxophonists
summary: He discusses duo and multi-baritone records with Pepper Adams, Cecil Payne, Ronnie Cuber, Gary Smulyan, and 24 baritones at Carney's memorial.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well you’ve been able to get together with some of your contemporaries on the baritone on some of your records, right?

Oh, yeah. I recorded a duo, the first time I ever did it was with Pepper Adams and then we did one with three baritones, Cecil Payne and Ronnie Cuber. And I just did one three months ago with three baritones — Ronnie Cuber, Gary Smulyan and myself, and we did the music of Gerry Mulligan. And we took all Mulligan tunes. And maybe Gerry would roll over in his grave if he heard us playing it, but it was some interesting things. You know, with three different guys playing Mulligan’s music, of all the musics. But one baritone is bad enough, we don’t need three. It was a fun experience, let’s put it that way. I always enjoyed, it’s like having — one time I remember we had, Harry Carney died and we had twenty-four baritones and a rhythm section at St. Peter’s Cathedral. Most of the people there just owned the horns, maybe about six of us could play. But just to see that many baritones.
Like wow. But it was like a sound I don’t really cherish.
